security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel writes to mip/mie CSRs assuming no WARL-induced bit modifications (i.e., without read-back verification), or context-switch save/restore of mie/mip relies on write-exact-semantics — if hardware silently drops unsupported interrupt bits on write, the kernel operates on false interrupt-enable state (e.g., MTIE cleared means the hardclock scheduler tick never fires); additionally, in bhyve two-stage translation, an incorrect assumption about whether a misaligned access raises a misaligned exception before or after a VS-stage page fault priority can cause the hypervisor to emulate the wrong fault.
security_spec.summary: mip/mie are WARL: kernel must read-back after write or risk silent interrupt-enable loss (hardclock dead); mcause VS-fault priority is impl-def: bhyve two-stage misaligned emulation fragile to ordering changes
